verdicts.claim: Headline: taehyun_xai_dirs is not a Cheon et al. 2025 reproduction (is_cheon_reproduction=false); both directories are byte-identical
verdicts.reason: The package exports only a post-hoc SHAP wrapper. Nothing in the six .py files or USAGE.md reads data, builds a cohort, splits folds, selects features, or trains/tunes a model. Greps for read_csv|read_excel|open(|Data/|aihub|MMSE|DIAG, for KFold|cross_val|train_test_split|forward|전진|Cheon, and for min_data_in_leaf|num_leaves|n_estimators|learning_rate|GridSearch|330|0.08 all return no match inside xai/. `diff -rq -x __pycache__ Taehyun/xai Taehyun/previous/xai` exits 0. Independently, the actual Cheon reproductions (Taehyun/Paper_Reproduction/Cheon_LGBM.py:262 and Paper_Reproduction_Nested/Cheon_LGBM.py:229) call `shap.TreeExplainer(...)` directly and never import xai, so this package is not on any Cheon path.

verdicts.reason: Code and docs describe exactly this scope, and none of the paper's pipeline stages exist in the package (see headline verdict). One small inaccuracy in the reader's evidence: no V25 file references ShapAnalyzer — the repo-wide grep shows callers Taehyun/Binary/{Binary_LGBM_RF, Binary_LGBM_RF_v2, V26, V27, V28, V29, V30, V35, V36, V37, V41}.py, Taehyun/Model/Binary/*.py (V26–V41 incl. verdicts.claim: Deviation 2 — Default task and class count: task='multiclass', n_classes=3 with class names CN/MCI/Dementia; paper is binary CN=0 vs MCI+Dem=1
verdicts.reason: The code defaults are exactly task="multiclass", n_classes=3. Nuance: the CN/MCI/Dementia names are only in USAGE.md examples; the code default is ["class_0","class_1","class_2"] (analyzer.py:93-97). Also, task="binary" affects two places, not one: the class-axis slicing (analyzer.py:306-307) and the save_plots branch (analyzer.py:205, per-class plots only when task == "multiclass"). Importantly, every real caller overrides the default with task="binary", n_classes=1 (e.g. Taehyun/Binary/V26_Binary_SOTA_Optimization.py:87, V41_Binary_MMSE_Based.py:132, Taehyun/Model/Binary/V31_MultiSHAP_Consensus.py:75, Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:155), so the 'multiclass default' is a documentation-level deviation only.

verdicts.claim: Potential error 1 — task='binary' with an older shap returning a list of two arrays: _to_ndarray stacks to (2,N,F); _slice_classes returns it unchanged; aggregate_time_axis treats axis 1 (samples) as time; importance_dataframe then averages the two class slices so mean_signed_shap collapses to 0 while mean_abs_shap stays correct
verdicts.reason: The shape-handling chain is exactly as described: list -> np.stack axis=0 -> (2,N,F); non-multiclass returns [raw] untouched; a 3-D array is collapsed along axis 1 regardless of whether that axis is time or samples. Two corrections to the stated consequence, however. (a) Under the DEFAULT aggregation="abs_mean", np.abs is applied at aggregation.py:47 BEFORE importance_dataframe, so the (2,F) input is non-negative and mean_signed_shap equals mean_abs_shap — it does NOT collapse to 0. The 'collapses to 0' outcome occurs only with aggregation="mean"/"sum" (sign preserved, slice 1 = −slice 0), and in those modes mean_abs_shap is |mean_n shap| rather than mean_n |shap|, i.e. also not 'correct'. So neither aggregation mode matches the reader's full description, but the underlying axis-confusion defect is real. (b) The path is only reachable with n_classes=1 (or a one-element class_names): for task="binary" sliced has length 1 (analyzer.py:307) while per_class_values indexes sliced[i] for every class name (analyzer.py:148) and the length check at :98 is skipped for non-multiclass — so n_classes=2 raises IndexError first. The real callers do use n_classes=1 (V26:87, V31:75, V41:132, Binary_LGBM_RF.py:155), so the scenario is reachable in practice if an old shap is installed; whether any caller ran under such a version cannot be determined from the code.
verdicts.evidence: explainers.py:81-82 `if isinstance(raw, list):` / `return np.stack([np.asarray(r) for r in raw], axis=0)`; analyzer.py:306-307 `if task != "multiclass":` / `return [raw]`; aggregation.py:46-47 `if mode == "abs_mean":` / `return np.mean(np.abs(shap_values), axis=1)`; outputs.py:50,52 `mean_abs = np.mean(np.abs(shap_2d), axis=0)` / `mean_signed = np.mean(shap_2d, axis=0)`; analyzer.py:148 `return {name: sliced[i] for i, name in enumerate(self.class_names)}`

verdicts.claim: Potential error 2 — For tree models SHAP importance is computed on whatever X the caller passes; the package has no notion of train/test folds, so any leakage (ranking on evaluation rows) is decided by the calling script
verdicts.reason: explain(X) coerces X and hands it straight to TreeExplainer.shap_values; there is no fold, split, or seed logic anywhere in the package (only `random_state` for Keras background sampling, analyzer.py:259). Additional evidence beyond the USAGE.md examples: the real callers pass `X_res` (V26:88, V41:133, V31:76) or `X_train` (Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:156), not `X_test` — so what rows are explained (and whether X_res is a resampled training set) is entirely caller-determined and not auditable from xai/.
verdicts.evidence: analyzer.py:112 `def explain(self, X) -> "ShapAnalyzer":`; analyzer.py:118-122 `if self.model_type == "tree":` / `self._adapter = TreeAdapter(self.model)` / `shap_input = X_pandas if X_pandas is not None else X_arr` / `self._raw_shap = self._adapter.shap_values(shap_input)`; explainers.py:42 `raw = self.explainer.shap_values(X)`; USAGE.md:45 `analyzer.explain(X_test)`; Taehyun/Binary/V26_Binary_SOTA_Optimization.py:87-88 `ShapAnalyzer(model=base_model, feature_names=features, task="binary", n_classes=1, class_names=["Abnormal"])` / `analyzer.explain(X_res)`

missed_items: SHAP explainer mode reported without code evidence: the reader states 'tree_path_dependent', but explainers.py:39 is just `self.explainer = shap_lib.TreeExplainer(model)` — no `feature_perturbation` and no `data` argument. The perturbation mode is therefore whatever the installed shap version does when no background is supplied (historically a silent fallback to tree_path_dependent); it is a runtime/library inference, not a choice fixed in this code. Same for the reader's shap<0.45 'list output' premise — no shap version is pinned anywhere in xai/ (no requirements file; USAGE.md:19 only says `pip install shap`).

Actual usage configuration not reported: every real caller instantiates `ShapAnalyzer(..., task="binary", n_classes=1, class_names=["Abnormal"])` (or ["Dementia"]) — Taehyun/Binary/V26_Binary_SOTA_Optimization.py:87, V41_Binary_MMSE_Based.py:132, Taehyun/Model/Binary/V31_MultiSHAP_Consensus.py:75, Taehyun/Binary_LGBM_RF.py:155. A grep for `n_classes=3` outside USAGE.md finds nothing. The 'multiclass default' deviation is documentation-only.

Crash the reader missed: task="binary" with the natural n_classes=2 raises IndexError. analyzer.py:307 returns a one-element list for any non-multiclass task, analyzer.py:148 indexes `sliced[i]` for every entry of class_names (length n_classes), and the length guard at analyzer.py:98 applies only when task == "multiclass". n_classes=1 is the only configuration under which the binary path runs — which is why all callers use it.

Second binary failure route (version-dependent, not run here): with shap >= 0.45 a binary sklearn RandomForestClassifier returns (N, F, 2); for task="binary" this 3-D array reaches aggregate_time_axis (aggregation.py:39-47), is collapsed along axis 1 (= features) to (N, 2), and importance_dataframe then raises `Feature count mismatch` (outputs.py:43-47). LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost binary return (N, F) and are unaffected. Cannot be confirmed without running; flagged as unclear.

Class-averaged plot may be degenerate: analyzer.py:216 `stacked = np.mean(np.stack(list(per_class_vals.values()), axis=0), axis=0)` averages SIGNED per-class SHAP for tree models (aggregate_time_axis returns 2-D tree SHAP unchanged, aggregation.py:36-37). For explainers whose per-class SHAP sums to zero across classes (probability-output models such as sklearn RandomForest), this average is identically 0, so `save_plots(per_class=False)` would draw an all-zero plot. Reasoned from the code, not executed — treat as unclear.
`to_dataframe(combine_classes=False)` silently drops mean_signed_shap: analyzer.py:179-182 aggregates only `mean_abs_shap=("mean_abs_shap", "mean")`. Minor, unreported.

No column-name check between a DataFrame input and `feature_names`: analyzer.py:289-290 returns a DataFrame untouched, and the only validation is the length check at outputs.py:43-47. A column-order mismatch would silently mislabel features in the importance table. Minor, unreported.

Keras background defaults to a sample of the explained set itself: analyzer.py:257-264 draws `background_size` (default 100, analyzer.py:69) rows from X_arr with `np.random.default_rng(self.random_state)` (default 42, analyzer.py:71) when `background` is None — i.e. from X_test if X_test is what is explained. The reader mentioned the seed but not that the background comes from the explained rows.

Reader's caller list is slightly off: 'V25' does not exist among callers (grep shows V26–V41); Hyunsoo/previous/privious_TreeModel_preprocessing/model/LGBM_RF_Model_ver2.py:47 (`from xai import ShapAnalyzer`, optional fallback) is an additional caller the reader omitted. The SangHyo/Reproduction/XAI_Paper_Reproduction/scripts/*.py hits are a different package (`from xai_paper_reproduction import ...`), and Hyunsoo/reproduction_audit/code/run_experiment.py:7 explicitly says the custom xai.ShapAnalyzer was not available locally and standard shap was used instead — so neither is a consumer of this package.

Independence of the orchestrator pointer not established by the reader: Taehyun/Paper_Reproduction/Cheon_LGBM.py:11,262 and Taehyun/Paper_Reproduction_Nested/Cheon_LGBM.py:15,229 `import shap` / `shap.TreeExplainer(...)` directly and never import xai. Hence nothing in the audited xai/ package influences the actual Cheon reproductions.
